candidate_relations.label: Intra-atrial Re-entrant Tachycardia
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record shows QRS complexes outnumbering P waves in a 3:2 ratio (VA dissociation pattern favoring ventricular origin), RBBB morphology with left-axis deviation (classic left posterior fascicular VT pattern), cannon A waves (AV dissociation), and EP study confirming the tachycardia origin. These features are incompatible with an atrial re-entrant mechanism, which would show P waves driving QRS complexes, not the reverse. The reference diagnosis of left posterior fascicular VT is supported by the narrow-ish QRS with RBBB+LAD morphology and verapamil responsiveness history.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Atrial re-entrant tachycardia is a supraventricular mechanism; the reference is a ventricular tachycardia of fascicular origin

case_quality_flags: 3:2 relationship described as QRS outnumbering P waves is consistent with VA dissociation or 3:2 VA conduction from VT, supporting fascicular VT over any atrial mechanism
Verapamil-sensitive tachycardia with RBBB+left-axis deviation is pathognomonic for left posterior fascicular VT
